statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail eases further inside the low band because the 29,116.75 overnight low has held since the early European hours and roughly 60% of the decline is retraced, while Stress stays elevated on live 50% US tariffs on selected Canadian goods, a two-decade-high 30-year yield and the 18:00Z Treasury press conference detailing new Iran measures.
recommendation: Descriptive: NQ near 29,232 (-0.53%) at 10:09Z is holding a 29,117-29,297 range with the overnight low untested for several hours, which is the opposite of the repeated extension after failed retracements that would threaten a mean-reversion basket. ES -0.19% and YM -0.02% keep the weakness tech-specific, Treasury futures are bid across the curve and WTI is 2.3% lower near $85 despite Iran escalation rhetoric, so no cross-asset amplifier is aligned. The narrow mapped danger window spans the 13:30Z US cash open through 14:30Z, where opening-auction retracement quality is the decisive evidence, with a secondary checkpoint at the 18:00Z sanctions press conference. Tail remains well below the block threshold.
headline: Nasdaq-100: overnight low holds through the European morning; Tail eases within the low band, Stress stays elevated
body: NQ futures traded at 29,232.00, down 0.53%, at 10:09Z against a 29,387.75 prior close, inside an unchanged 29,116.75-29,297.00 range. The decisive observation since the prior assessment is that the range has compressed rather than extended: the overnight low set in the early European hours has not been retested, roughly 60% of the decline remains retraced, and the last hour produced no new extreme. Repeated extension after failed retracements is the pattern that overwhelms a mean-reversion basket, and the opposite is being observed. Cross-asset confirmation stays absent. ES is 0.19% lower near 7,677, YM is 0.02% lower at 53,340 and European cash indices are flat, so the weakness remains tech-specific rather than a broad risk-off repricing. The latest H.15 constant-maturity readings are 4.19% at 2 years, 4.69% at 10 years and 5.23% at 30 years, and Treasury futures are bid from the 2-year through the long bond today, so the long end is not the source of the equity pressure. WTI is 2.3% lower near $85 and Brent around $91.5, a disinflationary offset rather than an amplifier, and notably no supply premium is priced even after Iran warned that shipping in the Strait of Hormuz could be targeted; reporting notes tanker transits actually increased late last week. Gold is 0.5% higher near $4,705 and bitcoin is firm, consistent with debasement hedging rather than an equity-liquidation path. VIX is near 15.9, roughly one point above Friday's 14.89 close and far from a regime shift. The drag is concentrated in semiconductors, where the latest session left MU 3.4% lower, ARM 2.2% lower, AMD 1.7% lower and AVGO 0.9% lower while NVDA was marginally higher; the megacap set was mixed with five of eight higher, which is dispersion rather than aligned selling. The macro backdrop supplies the elevated Stress rather than the Tail: Canada suspended trade negotiations and 50% US tariffs on more than $20bn of Canadian goods are in motion with matching retaliation pledged, and Treasury Secretary Bessent holds a 14:00 ET press conference detailing an expanded Iran sanctions campaign aimed at foreign banks, shippers and oil buyers. Both are recognised, priced catalysts rather than unresolved discontinuities. Today's only US release is the Chicago Fed National Activity Index at 12:30Z. The week's dominant catalyst is Nvidia's report after the close on 26 August, preceded by Core PCE, the second GDP estimate and durable goods that morning, with the Jackson Hole symposium and the Fed Chair keynote on 28 August. Tail is therefore held at 11 in the low band, Stress at 49 in the elevated band, and the narrow mapped danger window is retained across the 13:30Z-14:30Z US cash open, where the opening auction supplies the first genuinely new price-path evidence.

lookbackSummary: Over the prior 24 clock-hours the published Claude series stayed green with EA_ON throughout. Tail held at 4 across the 23 August US session while Stress climbed from 36 to 45, then stepped to 15 at 22:00Z as the Asian tech decline began and settled into a 7-12 band overnight. The Asian weakness peaked in the published series at 07:00Z with Tail 19 and Stress 58 on a trend-down mode, eased to Tail 17 at 08:00Z, and turned to a mixed mode at 09:00Z with Tail 12 and Stress 50 once the retracement was observed. Three hours on 23 August, 10:00Z, 11:00Z and 12:00Z, have no published assessment and are marked unavailable.
outlookSummary: The 24-hour path holds Tail in the low band and the EA_ON mapping for every hour except the 13:00Z and 14:00Z US cash-open window, where conditional Tail steps to 20 and maps to WATCH around the 13:30Z-14:30Z danger window. Stress stays elevated through the US session, peaking at 60 during the 18:00Z Iran sanctions press conference, which is scored as headline whipsaw risk rather than an assumed outcome. Conditional risk then decays through the US close on the assumption of orderly price discovery, bottoms with Stress in the low 40s overnight, and edges back up through Tuesday's Asian and European sessions as the 25 August US calendar and Wednesday's Nvidia report come into view.
